It is faith that does not work by love, which is a dead faith, resting on formalities without spirit and life.

"Is not the LORD among us?" Are we not in the city of Jerusalem, the city of God? Are not His temple and the ark of His covenant and His holy book and His priests and His daily sacrifices in our hands? Thus they misused the divine privileges offered to them for their sanctification, so they abandoned holiness and held fast to formalities.

The gifts of God to them were diverted from their purpose, so they imagined that God was in their midst as long as they had these gifts, even though they persisted in the love of the world, injustice and violence.
Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest. [12]

This prophecy had its effective impact more than a century later, when the prophet Jeremiah quoted it (Jer 26:18), and it had a deep impression on Jeremiah. Its quotation led to the saving of Jeremiah's life when he was exposed to the danger of being put to death in the days of Jehoiakim.

They claimed that they were building Zion and caring for its constructions ]10[, not knowing that while they care for the streets and the magnificent buildings they are working for the ruin of the holy places.

If the leaders thought that since God was in their midst no destruction would come upon them, then because of their insistence on seizing fields God allows the destruction of Zion, so that its buildings are scattered, and turn into fields and ruins and desolation! What befalls Zion reveals what befalls the depths of these wicked ones, and what will also befall as the fruit of their insistence on evil, hiding behind the presence of Zion and the temple of the Lord as a sign of God's dwelling in their midst.

* Here also the divine Micah was unable to bear one in Zion in whom blood flows, which is interpreted to mean that Jerusalem is stained with injustice. While the heads of the house of Jacob were disgusted with justice, the priests taught for hire. The prophets prophesied for money! What does Micah say of the result of this? "Zion shall be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become as a storehouse of fruit (ruined), and the mountain of the house as a wooded grove." He also lamented the lack of uprightness, so that a stalk (of plant) or a trace of grapes is rare, since the prince asks and the judge flatters (Mic 7:1-4). His language often resembled the mighty saying of David: "Save me, O Lord, for the righteous has failed" (Ps 12:1). So their good things will come to an end, for "thou hast consumed like the moth that which is desirable" (Ps 12:1).
St. Gregory of Nazianzus Some see that this prophecy was fulfilled literally at the hand of Titus, when the Romans plowed the land on which the city stood so that total ruin might be accomplished.
Let me know the truth, that I may become a leader!
* My soul trembles at hearing of the wicked leaders.
They thought that they knew the truth and defended it.
And they are far from knowing it!
You are the divine Truth; open my eyes that I may know You, let me walk in You, that I may live forever!
* Grant me to love the good and hate the evil.
Let me love the good, whatever its cost, and hate the evil, whatever its enticements!
* Let me love the good for every human being, that I may love You, O Lover of mankind!
Remove from me all covetousness, greed and selfishness; remove from me violent brutality.
Grant me self-giving, free love.
Let me love and not seek to be loved.
For I love You even in those who oppose me.
* Let me show compassion to others, that You may show compassion to me.
Let me respond to the requests of others, that You may hear my voice and answer my prayers.
* Remove from me all hypocrisy, that I may go forth in the truth without flattery!
Let me please You, and not seek the approval of men.
I cling to You, and You shine upon me with Your light that I may know Your will, and be enlightened by the splendor of Your righteousness.
My whole life becomes day without night, and light without darkness, and love without hatred!
* Grant me the power of Your Holy Spirit, that I may be filled with power, truth and might.
Let me speak the truth, whatever its cost, and not flatter a rich man or one in authority!
Let me speak Your words without distortion!
* Let me worship You in spirit and truth, that formalities without spirit may not swallow me up!
Let me perceive Your indwelling and Your dwelling in me!
Then You establish the spiritual Zion, and sanctify my depths as a temple for You.

1 But in the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of the LORD shall be established in the top of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills; and people shall flow unto it.

The prophet Micah looks toward the fullness of time, when God the Word becomes incarnate to raise up from humanity not a lofty mountain like Mount Horeb, where the prophet Moses received the Law, but the mountain of mountains, whose summit reaches heaven itself. For the Heavenly One came to raise up from the fallen a glorious Church of towering height, bearing the citizenship of her heavenly Bridegroom.

An American child, proud of his nationality, wrote a letter addressed to God, in which he said: "I am an American, and what about You?" He is the Heavenly One who calls every believer to be united with Him and to bear His citizenship, so that all sing with the Apostle Paul: "[He] hath made us sit together in heavenly places."

But in the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of the LORD shall be established in the top of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills; and people shall flow unto it. [1]

What is stated in verses [1-3] is almost identical to what is stated in the Book of Isaiah (Isa 2:2-4). Since the two were contemporaries, though Isaiah was older than Micah, some think that the latter quoted this from the former, while some scholars think that both quoted from a third source, under the guidance of the Holy Spirit of God.
The expression "in the last days" is usually used by the prophets to point to the messianic age (Hos 3:5).

* (The prophet Isaiah 2:2) He prophesies of a glorious and widespread manifestation of godliness among all who dwell round about: the destruction of the idols, with the house of the Lord enjoying the universal character that befits it. For by the mountains and hills he means not only the removal of the errors that had reigned over everyone, after the appearing of our Savior, when the falsehood of the idols was exposed, but he also announced the beauty of the truth, and thus we see the prophecy being fulfilled. Add to this the saying "in the last days," by which he means "the days that follow the appearing of the Lord."

Theodoret, Bishop of Cyrus. Many of the Fathers of the Church see that this glorious mountain refers to the Church of the New Testament, among them St. Cyril the Great, St. John Chrysostom and Eusebius of Caesarea.

* Paul said the same thing: "The fullness of the time was come" (Gal 4:4), and in another place: "that in the dispensation of the fulness of times" (Isa 2:2). He points to the Church and the firmness of her teachings like a mountain... What is marvelous about the Church is not that she is victorious, but the manner in which she became so. She is pursued and persecuted, and torn in a thousand ways, and yet not only does she not diminish, but she has become great, and by enduring sufferings she shatters those who try to pour blows upon her. This is the work of the pearl that is struck with iron: it exhausts the strength of those who strike it... So when the prophet depicts her as a mountain, he means by this the strength of the Church, her steadfastness, her loftiness and her endurance...

"And all nations shall flow unto it." Notice here how the prophet not only announced the call directed to the Gentiles, but also their eagerness to respond to the call. He did not say "they will be driven," but "they will come."
St. John Chrysostom. Is not all humanity, the one flock, God's? Is not God Himself the Lord of all peoples and their Shepherd?

Tertullian the scholar. The Church is raised to the top of the mountains, that is, she reaches the heights of heaven, where she bears the heavenly nature by her union with the heavenly Head. And she is exalted above the hills, where she passes over every earthly standard and human thought, rising above all human philosophies, cultures and arts, for she is not the making of men, but the work of the hands of the Almighty Himself.

"People shall flow unto it": this does not apply to the Jewish temple, which was closed to the Gentiles; but the Church, from the very beginning of her going forth, the Lord called His disciples to go and teach the nations (Mt 28:19).

Some of the Fathers see that the mountain of the house of the Lord is the Lord Christ, who is established in the top of the mountains, that is, above all the prophets. This mountain is the rock on which the Church of the New Testament is founded.
* The prophet Micah presented Christ under the symbol of a great mountain, speaking thus: "But in the last days the mountain of the house of the LORD..." (Mic 4:2-3).
St. Augustine

entries.section: 2. A people of peoples and a divine school:

paragraphs.text: 2 And many nations shall come, and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

The Jews considered that there was no salvation for anyone unless he became a Jew, and that all the other peoples had no relationship with God, since they alone were the chosen people of God. They did not realize that God, who chose them to be a holy leaven, chose all the nations to ascend, with Christ who ascended into the heavens, to the mountain of the Lord, to heaven itself.

If God raises up from every believing heart a holy temple for Himself, it is only so that the Law of the New Testament may go forth from Jerusalem, the word of the Lord that attracts every tongue and nation, so that all may enjoy the Word, the Giver of life and resurrection. The Church has become the people of peoples, gathering from all the nations a holy, heavenly people.
She is a divine school whose head is the unique divine Teacher; He carries His disciples in Himself and dwells in their depths, so that they receive fellowship in the divine nature.
And many nations shall come, and say,
Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths:
for the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem. [2]

The nations will come to the Church of the New Testament, the mountain of the Lord and the house of the God of Jacob, so that all may enjoy the prophecies and types in the Law concerning the Lord Christ and His work of salvation.

In the letter of Pope Athanasius to Epictetus, bishop of Jerusalem, he quotes this passage to speak of the coming of the incarnate Word of the Lord from Jerusalem, explaining that the Word was not changed into flesh and bones and hair and the whole body, nor did He change from His divine nature by His incarnation.

* From here (Jerusalem) every place in the world has experienced joy; from here come happiness and delight, from here the sources of sound thought; here Christ was crucified, and from here the Apostles set out... This delight is immortal.

St. John Chrysostom. * The prophet Micah used the symbol of the high mountain to speak of the gathering of the nations in Christ [he cites (Mic 4:1-3)]... After that the same prophet told us beforehand even the place where Christ was born (Mic 5:2).

St. Augustine. * Micah announced that the new Law would be given in the following way: "The law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem. And he shall judge among many people, and shall conquer nations and rebuke them." For the first Law, which was given through Moses, was not given on Mount Zion but on Mount Horeb. And the Sibyl showed that this would come to an end through the Son of God. "But when all these things are fulfilled of which he spoke at that time, the whole Law (in its letter) will be abolished."

Lactantius. * When the prophetic Spirit spoke, prophesying of the things to come, he said: "The law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem, and he shall judge among the nations, and many people shall be rebuked. And they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks, nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more." We can show you that this has indeed truly happened. For a company of twelve men went out from Jerusalem, who were common and untrained in speech. But by the power of God they bore witness to Christ in order to teach all the word of God. And now we who used to kill one another not only do not make war against one another, but, so as not to lie and not to deceive our judges, we gladly die for the confession of Christ; for it has become possible for us to follow the saying: "The tongue swears while the mind remains unsworn." But it is folly for the soldiers who were enlisted by you and whose names were registered to remain in loyalty to you instead of loyalty to their lives and their parents and their country and all their families. For you have nothing incorruptible to offer to those who desire incorruption. Rather we bear all things in order to receive what we desire from the One who is able to grant it.

St. Justin. * Behold, you see that they will be choirs and keep festivals, each encouraging the other, and all became teachers, not one nation nor two nor three nations... but all gather together. He says: many peoples came from different lands. This never happened at all with the Jews; if a few came, they were a few proselytes who came with great difficulty, and they never took the name of the nations, but came as proselytes.

St. John Chrysostom. * The great David says to you: "O come, let us rejoice in the Lord" (Ps 95:1), or another prophet says: "Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD" (Mic 4:2), or the Savior Himself says: "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest" (Mt 11:28), or: Arise for plunder, shining with splendor, gleaming more than snow, whiter than milk (see Lam 4:7), shining more than sapphire; let us not resist nor delay!

St. Gregory of Nazianzus. * After the experience of the troubles in which they will find themselves, when first the Assyrians and later the Babylonians take them captive, a great change will take place with regard to this place, the mountain that is thought to be where God dwells, as it becomes famous and is shown to surpass all mountains, to rise above all the mountains and hills because of the glory that covers it through divine compassion. Great numbers from all places, even from foreign peoples, will hasten to gather and reach the mountain of God, where God is thought to dwell, and they will learn how they ought to order their lives as is fitting.

Theodore of Mopsuestia. * The divine Gospel preaching reaches to the ends of the earth, according to the prophecy of the Lord recorded in the holy Gospels: "[This gospel of the kingdom] shall be preached ... for a witness unto all nations" [see Mt 24:14]. And He urged the holy Apostles with the words: "Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you" (Mt 28:19-20). This Gospel Law and Apostolic preaching began at Jerusalem as from a spring and reached the whole world, providing irrigation for those who draw near to the faith.

* "For the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem." The prophet speaks here of a new Law and a new word, because the old Law was given at Sinai, but the Law of the New Testament was delivered at Zion. The first was delivered to the Jews alone, but the new was delivered to all peoples and nations, to the whole human race. God gave the old Law not at Zion, but on Mount Sinai. It is very clear that he is pointing to the New Testament. There it was given first to the Apostles, and thanks to them, as they carried it to all the nations.
Theodoret, Bishop of Cyrus

3 And he shall judge among many people, and rebuke strong nations afar off; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

After speaking of the Church as the firm mountain of mountains, and as a unique school under the leadership of the divine Teacher, the Lord of glory Jesus, he tells us of her as a marvelous and unique court in which the Judge, the Savior of the world, is enthroned, not to destroy and take vengeance, but to renew human nature by His Holy Spirit, and so grant heavenly peace and surpassing harmony. Instead of the battle between soul and body, and between mind and human passions, His surpassing peace reigns over the whole being of man, so that he becomes a harp of the Spirit that sends forth a song of heavenly love, proclaiming the accomplishment of reconciliation with God, as with men and with the heavenly beings.
And he shall judge among many people,
and rebuke strong nations afar off; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks:
nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more. [3]
* Since the coming of the Lord, the New Testament has restored peace, and the Law that gives life has gone forth to all the earth, as the prophets said.

St. Irenaeus. * Who is this that does so, or who is it that unites men in peace, who hated one another, except the beloved Son of the Father, the common Savior of all, Jesus Christ, who by His love undertook all things for our salvation? For from of old the peace that He brings in was foretold, as the Scripture says: "They shall beat their swords into plowshares."

Pope Athanasius the Apostolic. What are these swords but the passions, feelings and energies which we used to use to kill our souls and the souls of those attached to us? For through the spiritual peace that the Savior grants us, all these energies are turned into plowshares for our souls, which till our hearts, removing the stones and thorns and turning our inner wilderness into a spiritual garden full of the fruit of the Spirit.
Man no longer learns war against his brother, but enjoys peace without fear (Zech 3:10).

4 But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid: for the mouth of the LORD of hosts hath spoken it. 5 For all people will walk every one in the name of his god, and we will walk in the name of the LORD our God for ever and ever.

The Lord planted the garden of Eden so that Adam and his sons might live under the tree of life, to eat and be satisfied, and to sit and rest in the Lord. But man soon drove himself out of the garden to live in the valley of tears, groaning under the weight of the sin he chose with his full free will, and he became its abject slave. Now that our Christ has come, He has established His Church as a joyful divine garden, in which His sons (the sons of the second Adam) may live. The believer sits under the vine and rests under the fig tree. What is the vine but the Lord Christ, crucified and risen from the dead, the source of true joy, the wine of the New Testament? And what is the fig tree but the Holy Spirit, the Giver of love, who binds believers together like the seeds of the fig, which give a sweet taste and are enclosed in a covering of unity that holds the seeds within?
It is a unique garden in which we eat and drink of the Body and Blood of the Lord, and are watered by His Holy Spirit, the living water!
But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid: for the mouth of the LORD of hosts hath spoken it. [4]

Sitting under the shade is a symbolic expression used to indicate the peace of the nation and local happiness (see 1 Kgs 4:25; Zech 3:10). This was based on the custom that prevailed, that a person would seek a pleasant shade under fig trees and vines. In the East the vine is used more for ornament and for shade than ivy in the West. The branches are trained to make a trellis in the courtyard of the house. Fig trees, with their massive branches and broad leaves, provide a natural shade that delights the soul.

* The Song of Songs alludes to (the vine and the fig tree of the field) in this way: "I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and virtues of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please" (Song 2:7) LXX.

This is the field (of righteousness) full of peace itself, of which the Lord also speaks in the Psalm: "Whatsoever moves in the field is mine" (Ps 50:11) LXX. In this field is the vine that is pressed and gives forth blood, and washes and purifies the world. And in this field is the tree under which the saints sit to rest, and are renewed by good spiritual grace. In this field the fruitful olive tree is crushed, and gives the oil of the Lord's peace. In this field the pomegranate trees (Song 8:2) flourish, shading much fruit in the bosom of the one faith and sending into it the warmth of love.

St. Ambrose. * The vine in not a few places refers to the Lord Himself (Jn 15:1), and the fig tree to the Holy Spirit, since the Lord "makes glad the heart of man" (Ps 104:5), and the Holy Spirit heals it. Hezekiah was commanded to make a plaster of a lump of figs, that is, of the fruit of the Spirit, so that he might be healed. And as the Apostle says of this healing, it begins with love: "But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance" (Gal 5:22-23). Because of the greatness of their delight, the prophet calls these spiritual fruits figs. Micah also says of them: "They shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid" (Mic 4:4). Surely whoever takes refuge in the Spirit and rests under Him, and under the shadow of the Word, is not frightened or terrified by anyone who causes trouble to human hearts.

Methodius. * We read in Genesis that God planted a garden eastward, and there He put the man whom He had formed (Gen 2:8). Who has the power to create a paradise but God Almighty, who "spake, and it was done" (Ps 33:9), and who never had need of what He willed to bring into being? He planted this paradise, of which He says that it is His wisdom: "Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up" (Mt 15:13). It is a good planting, for it was said of the angels and the saints that they rest under the fig tree and the vine. In this matter there is a symbol of the angels in the time of the peace to come.
St. Ambrose. For all people will walk every one in the name of his god, and we will walk in the name of the LORD our God for ever and ever.
Those who walk in the name of the Lord will have eternal peace. [5]

* Those who are eager to ascend the mountain of the Lord, and desire to learn His ways, promise readiness for obedience, and so receive within them the glories of life in Christ, and pledge with all their strength to be zealous in all holiness. He says: "In every country and city let each one walk in the way he chooses and worship as seems good to him; but our concern is Christ, and we make His law a straight path, in which we walk with Him, not only in this present life or in the past but, what is greater, in what lies beyond it." It is a faithful saying: "Those who suffer with Him will walk with Him forever, and with Him be glorified, and with Him reign" (see 2 Tim 2:11-12; Rom 8:17). But those who prefer nothing to His love make Christ their concern; these cease from the distraction of the vain world and seek rather righteousness and what is pleasing to Him, and to excel in virtue. Such was Paul, when he wrote: "I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me" (Gal 2:19-20). And again: "For I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified" (1 Cor 2:2).
St. Cyril the Great
6 In that day, saith the LORD, will I assemble her that halteth, and I will gather her that is driven out, and her that I have afflicted;

The wisdom of God incarnate was accused of being out of His mind, and was driven out of the camp to be crucified outside Jerusalem. There He stretched out His hands to embrace everyone who is broken, wounded, crushed and outcast! He is the Lord of the rejected. His own did not receive Him, that He might receive within Himself those who have nowhere to lay their heads. He is the Father of the fatherless, the Judge of the widows, the support of the persecuted, and the refuge of those who have no one to ask after them.
In that day, saith the LORD, will I assemble her that halteth, and I will gather her that is driven out, and her that I have afflicted; [6]
Here he prophesies of the return from captivity, when the nation had become outcast. After the chastening the Lord brings back the outcasts and binds up their wounds.
The outcasts become a chosen remnant, the strong people of God (Isa 37:32; 46:3; Jer 23:3; Amos 5:15).

7 And I will make her that halted a remnant, and her that was cast far off a strong nation: and the LORD shall reign over them in mount Zion from henceforth, even for ever. 8 And thou, O tower of the flock, the strong hold of the daughter of Zion, unto thee shall it come, even the first dominion; the kingdom shall come to the daughter of Jerusalem.

The prophet Ezekiel marveled when he saw the dry bones become an exceeding great army (Ezek 37:10). It is a vision of every day, in which the Lord Christ raises up from the weak, the ignorant and the despised a great tower that shelters the flock and protects it from the ravening wolves, and a great hill on which the serpent cannot crawl to strike its fangs into the heel of the children of God, and a royal throne on which the King of kings is enthroned to reign over the daughter of the heavenly Jerusalem, His holy Church.

* Now it is clear that no one in the whole world can frighten us or subdue us who believe in Jesus. Even though our heads are cut off and we are crucified and thrown to wild beasts and bound and burned, and endure every other kind of torture, it is evident that we do not deny the confession of our faith.

The more we are persecuted, the more the number of those who receive the faith increases and become worshippers of God in the name of Jesus. Just as one cuts off the branches of a fruitful vine and it grows again and puts forth other fruitful shoots, so it happens with the Christians, for the vine is planted by God and Christ is the Savior of His people. But the rest of the prophecy will be fulfilled at the Second Coming. The prophet Micah says: "In that day, saith the LORD, will I assemble her that halteth (the bruised), and I will gather her that is driven out, and her that I have rejected." This indicates that you do not have the last word, when you and all the other people who have authority wished to drive every Christian out not only from his possessions but even from the whole world, since you do not allow a Christian man to live.
St. Justin the Martyr. And I will make her that halted a remnant, and her that was cast far off a strong nation: and the LORD shall reign over them in mount Zion from henceforth, even for ever. [7]
And thou, O tower of the flock, the strong hold of the daughter of Zion, unto thee shall it come, even the first dominion; the kingdom shall come to the daughter of Jerusalem. [8]
When Jerusalem returns to greater splendor and strength, she becomes like a high tower from which the Good Shepherd tends His flock.

* "And thou, O tower, shepherd of the standing daughter of Zion, thy time shall come." These words refer to Zedekiah, the impious king, whom the prophet calls a tower because the people of Judah settled under his shade, and he calls him a shepherd because of his governance of the kingdom, and he calls him dark because of the error of idolatry to which he clung. Again, in the symbolic meaning of his words, he calls Satan a dark shepherd, for in a symbolic way he was always attacking the daughter of Zion under a dark sky. And when he hunts her he drags her away from the light, for truly he who walks in wickedness hates the light. But in the end the lofty, rightful Prince of the symbolic Jerusalem broke this tyrant by His coming, when He drew the dark shepherd away.
St. Ephrem the Syrian

9 Now why dost thou cry out aloud? is there no king in thee? is thy counsellor perished? for pangs have taken thee as a woman in travail. 10 Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail: for now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon; there shalt thou be delivered; there the LORD shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies. 11 Now also many nations are gathered against thee, that say, Let her be defiled, and let our eye look upon Zion. 12 But they know not the thoughts of the LORD, neither understand they his counsel: for he shall gather them as the sheaves into the floor.

If the Church is exposed to continual persecutions, so that she appears as one taken captive, yet her Bridegroom is the Redeemer, who saves her from her enemy, as He brought the ancient people out of Egypt and freed them from the slavery of Pharaoh. And as He brought His people back from the Babylonian captivity with a strong and wondrous hand!

Since the Jews interpreted God's promise to King David that his offspring would reign forever, they thought that Judah would never lack a king from the offspring of David. Therefore the words of the prophet Micah about the Babylonian captivity, a century and a half before it happened, were extremely alarming, especially since the false prophets were proclaiming smooth words, affirming God's protection of the city of Jerusalem and its unique temple and the continuance of the kingdom of David, who was of the tribe of Judah.
Now why dost thou cry out aloud?
is there no king in thee? is thy counsellor perished? for pangs have taken thee as a woman in travail. [9]

Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail: for now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon; there shalt thou be delivered;
there the LORD shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies. [10]

Salvation is accomplished through chastening, as God permits Jerusalem to be without a king, like a woman in labor who suffers to bring forth a new child. It was necessary for Judah to be taken captive to Babylon and then return, to enjoy freedom and the return to the land of promise.

* Writhe and groan, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in labor, "for now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the open country (the wilderness); and thou shalt go even to Babylon; there shalt thou be delivered." The meaning is that you will go into captivity, O (people of) Zion, you will be exiled in Babylon, but after years you will return from there, not with a soldier who hurries you along, but with that Commander who, by His ascent into heaven, leads captivity captive. You will follow Him with the brethren with hands joined, and with the commanders of our army who take captive every mind for the sake of Christ.
St. Ephrem the Syrian. Now also many nations are gathered against thee, that say,
Let her be defiled, and let our eye look upon Zion. [11]

When the pagan nations look at captive Jerusalem under chastening, they mock her and curse her, expecting her complete destruction. But these do not understand God's plan and His ordering. The nations will gather together against God and His people in a decisive battle (Joel 3; Ezek 38-39; Zech 12; Rev 20:8 etc.).

* Now many nations are gathered against thee. That is, at the same time a mixture of many different nations attacks you under the leadership of Gog. Again there will be a defiling in Zion, and the eye looks upon it, that is, the holy place of Zion will be defiled and utterly despised by those who do not know that they will be threshed by the vengeance of God's justice like the straw that is gathered on the threshing floor.
St. Ephrem the Syrian. But they know not the thoughts of the LORD, neither understand they his counsel: for he shall gather them as the sheaves into the floor. [12]
The prophet asks us not to search into future events out of a desire to satisfy our curiosity, but to learn the purposes and plans of the Lord concerning us.

13 Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion: for I will make thine horn iron, and I will make thy hoofs brass: and thou shalt beat in pieces many people: and I will consecrate their gain unto the LORD, and their substance unto the Lord of the whole earth.

The prophet David looked toward the Bridegroom of the Church, fairer than the children of men, and saw Him as a commander bearing His sword upon His thigh, going forth conquering and to conquer. Thus the bride of the Commander has her horn of iron and her hoofs of brass; she crushes the hosts of demons under her feet, and offers many souls to the Lord as true, surpassing riches.

Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion: for I will make thine horn iron, and I will make thy hoofs brass: and thou shalt beat in pieces many people: and I will consecrate their gain unto the LORD, and their substance unto the Lord of the whole earth. [13]
Now He gives us final victory, in which she crushes the enemy of good, and all events are turned to the glory of the Lord.

* "I will make thy horn, which the Babylonians broke, iron, and thou shalt beat in pieces many people, and thou shalt dedicate their produce to the Lord." This will happen after you possess their land and their wealth, and pay tithes to the Lord for the whole earth. As I said, God showed a sign of such great prosperity for the Jews who returned from the captivity. He has kept this very thing for the Church.
St. Ephrem the Syrian

entries.section: You have made Your people a wonder!

paragraphs.text: * Who is like You, O God, who forgive sins and give the Kingdom?
You have made of Your Church a wonder!
And You have shown Your power in me, as a member of Your unique Church!
* You have made of me, the weak and crushed, a lofty mountain, whose head is in heaven!
You have counted me Your fat mountain, the delight of the heavenly ones!
You are King of kings and Lord of lords; You have counted me the mountain of mountains, exceedingly high!
You have counted me a member of Your holy Church!
* You have made her a unique school with a heavenly Teacher.
She gathers disciples from every nation and people and tongue.
I have become a member in her, learning from You the language of heaven!
I speak the language of heavenly love by my fellowship with You, O Love. My soul praises You, for no fears come upon me.
In Your Church, the icon of heaven, I do not suffer from any inability in relationships.
For all learn in the language of love.
And none suffers from ignorance of the language or inability to speak.
You are wonderful, O heavenly Teacher!
You have made me beautiful in You, and I carry You within me.
You are in my heart as in my mouth; I speak of You continually!
* I no longer long for the garden of Eden like my father Adam.
For You have established for me a divine garden.
I pick the grapes of joy from You, O divine Vine!
I pick sweet, satisfying figs from Your Holy Spirit!
You have turned my depths into Your garden.
I see You with Your Father and Your Holy Spirit, the secret of my joy!
* I do not groan at the injustice that prevails in the world!
I see You driven out of the camp, and I find glory in being driven out with You, to bear Your cross!
You stretch out Your hands on the cross, and so embrace those who have no place in the hearts of others; You draw the poor, You who became poor to enrich us by Your poverty.
You draw the suffering, You who were crucified to give the sufferings of love a surpassing sweetness!
You embrace the lost, You who became the way that carries us to the divine bosom!
You receive the rejected to grant them fellowship in the heavenly glories!
* How often my soul has loathed my body because of its lusts!
How often my depths have groaned because of my trivial thoughts!
How often my heart has cried out because of my unruly passions!
Glory to You, O Sanctifier of my whole being!
You took a body that I might take pride in Your sanctification of my body!
You have given me Your Holy Spirit to govern my thoughts.
You have sanctified my passions and consecrated them as a throne for Your love!
You have established Your heavenly Kingdom in my depths!
You have turned my heart into Your radiant throne!
* Why art thou cast down, O my soul, within me? Hope in the Lord, the Redeemer!
Pharaoh has no authority to humble me, nor has Babylon the power to shut the doors of captivity upon me!
My Redeemer is the liberator of my soul, the Giver of victory to my depths!
* Behold, I see Satan fallen from heaven like lightning!
He has no place in me, for the Redeemer has made me a heaven!
I do not occupy my mind with you; you have no place except under my feet!
My Savior has given me authority over you, O weak one!
* My soul will lament no more, for my heavenly Bridegroom has made me a glorious Church!
He has made me, the dry bones, an exceeding great army!
In my Savior I have become Jerusalem, the army with banners!
Glory to You, O Bridegroom of the Church, her Savior and her Commander!
Now gather thyself in troops, O daughter of troops!
He hath laid siege against us:
they shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek. [1]
The call is addressed to the enemies of Zion, who had armies desiring victory over Israel and Judah, so that all her cities are besieged by divine permission to chasten His people.

The prophet Micah turns to what will befall Israel, when Assyria takes her captive, while Judah withstands the repeated siege of Assyria, until she is taken captive in stages, ending through Babylon in the days of King Zedekiah, and her complete ruin is accomplished at the hand of Titus in AD 70.

The king, the nobles and the religious leaders were preoccupied with wealth and power, and thought they were safe within the fortified walls of Jerusalem, and they did not realize that she would be besieged and destroyed, and that her judge or her king (Zedekiah) would be unable to protect her. Zedekiah, the last king of the offspring of David, was sitting on the throne of Jerusalem when Nebuchadnezzar seized it (2 Kgs 25:1).

* Thus he says that Samaria will be surrounded and besieged by hostile peoples. Not only will they strike her cheek with their heads, which could be borne, but they will crush her with staves, which carries a special cruelty. This means the humiliating, wretched ordeal of captivity, for without dispute a blow on the cheek carries a special insult. Notice that they also strike her with staves, causing violent troubles along with insult. Samaria was humiliated, since the tribe of Ephraim ruled her. She was in shame and under sufferings. In any case the striking hands will cease, and we shall not taste misery if we do what we can to remove the wrath of the Lord from all because of disobedience and the eager commission of sins, which the Lord hates. If instead of this we honor Him with a virtuous life, then we enjoy prosperity and live a joyful life worthy of praise.

St. Cyril the Great. Some see that the prophet Micah addresses his words here to the army of the Roman Titus, who besieged Jerusalem, because she struck her Judge, the Lord of glory Jesus, on the cheek, and insulted Him, saying: "Prophesy, who is it that smote thee?"

entries.section: 2. The birth of the eternal King:

paragraphs.text: 2 But thou, Beth-lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting. 3 Therefore will he give them up, until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth: then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel.

But thou, Beth-lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting. [2]

When the king is unable to protect Jerusalem and cannot save her, a marvelous king arises in a small village thought to be of no account among the thousands of villages of Judah, an eternal King who enters human history, able to save completely. The first dies and passes away in disgrace and shame, and the second reigns forever in the heavens, and His kingdom shall not pass away.

The expression "whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting" is unique to the Lord Christ alone, as the One eternally begotten, the only-begotten Son of God. For this reason He says: "Before Abraham was, I am" (Jn 8:58). And the Psalmist says: "From everlasting to everlasting, thou art God" (Ps 90:2).

Perhaps some may ask: How does he say, "that is to be ruler in Israel," when Israel condemned Him to crucifixion, and He did not set Himself up as king over Israel? He said: "My kingdom is not of this world" (Jn 18:36). He reigned over the new Israel, the holy Church, as "the head over all things to the church" (Eph 1:22). He displayed His authority over nature, and over death and diseases; was He then unable to reign over Israel? They wanted to make Him king, and He passed through the midst of them and they did not see Him!

Though both Israel and Judah fall into captivity, true reform is accomplished at the hand of the One born in Beth-lehem Ephratah, our Lord Jesus Christ. He is born in this humble place, in a village of His forefather, the great David.

Some tried to attribute this prophecy to Zerubbabel, but St. John Chrysostom explains that it does not apply to him. For on the one hand the prophet did not say "he will dwell in Beth-lehem" but "out of thee shall he come forth," and on the other hand Zerubbabel's goings forth are not "from of old, from everlasting"; rather it applies to Jesus Christ, the eternal Word.

In the dialogue of Tertullian the scholar with the Jews, he relies on this prophecy that was fulfilled literally in the person of Jesus Christ, and that now no one from the tribe of Judah from Beth-lehem remains in whom the prophecy could be fulfilled in another.
* Peace to Beth-lehem, the house of bread, in which was born the Bread that came down from heaven (Jn 6:51).
Peace to Ephratah, the land of fruitfulness and fertility, whose fruit is the Lord Himself.

Micah prophesied of you of old: "And thou Bethlehem... art not the least among the princes of Juda..." (Mt 2:6). For in you was born the Ruler, the One born before Lucifer. He whose birth from the Father is before time, and the cradle of the race of David continued in you until the Virgin brought forth her Son, and the remnant of the people who believed in Christ returned to the children of Israel preaching to them freely with words like these: "It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you: but seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles" (Acts 13:46).

St. Jerome. * He showed the truth as it is written of Jesus Christ, "though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor"; for this reason He chose a poor mother from whom He was born, and a poor homeland.

Origen the scholar. * It is not the divinity that came from Beth-lehem but the humanity, yet He did not stop at this point, but rather went forth from there with His divinity, as in the words "whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting."

St. John Chrysostom. * By designating the location of Beth-lehem, (the Jews) were like those who built Noah's ark, providing others with the means of escape while they themselves perished in the flood. They were like signposts that show the way but are unable to walk in it. They were asked: Where should Christ be born? They answered: "In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet" (Mt 2:5). They repeated from memory what had been written about this by Micah: "And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel" (Mt 2:6).

St. Augustine. * He who is before the ages, who was with God from the beginning, who is God the Word, whose origin is from the beginning, received birth according to the flesh in you (O Beth-lehem), and made you famous and radiant, though you are of no importance among the thousands of Judah.

* The blessed Apostle reminds us of the blessing of Judah, pointing out how it reached its fulfillment: "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda" (Heb 7:14). So also the prophet and the Evangelist Matthew. The former spoke prophesying, and the latter linked the prophecy to his story. What is strange in this, when he says that the evident enemies of the truth told Herod plainly that Christ would be born in Beth-lehem, since it is written: "And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel" (Mt 2:5-6). Let us add what the Jews omitted because of their malice, making the testimony incomplete (for they did not mention to Herod the rest of the prophecy). For the prophet, after saying "out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel," added "whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting" (Mic 5:2).

* By saying "out of thee shall come a Governor" he makes clear the economy of the Incarnation, and by adding "whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting" he proclaims His divinity, and that He is begotten of the Father before the ages.

entries.section: 2. The birth of the eternal King:

paragraphs.text: Theodoret, Bishop of Cyrus. Therefore will he give them up, until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth: then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel. [3]

The Lord gave them up to distress so that they might look for His coming, born of the Virgin, as the prophet Isaiah, a contemporary of the prophet Micah, prophesied of Him; and the latter specified the town of His birth.

With the coming of the King the Savior, the believing remnant returns to establish the Church of the New Testament, the new Israel. This holy remnant, which receives the Messiah the Savior, walks in the spirit of the fathers, the holy men of God. And so "the heart of the children to their fathers" is turned (Mal 4:6).

Some see that the "remnant" here refers not only to the believers from among the Jews but also from among the Gentiles, as all are joined to the fold of "the new children of Israel," as the Apostle Paul says: "And came and preached peace to you which were afar off, and to them that were nigh. For through him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father. Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God" (Eph 2:17-19).
And as the Jews are gathered together with the Gentiles in one faith, they become brethren to one another, "for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren" (Heb 2:11).

* He distinguishes between "them which were afar off, and them that were nigh" (Eph 2:17). This points to the Gentiles and the Jews. For the Jews are quite clearly nigh and the Gentiles afar off. Yet the Savior Himself brought the Gospel to the Gentiles. Paul indicates here first that Christ by His coming truly preached peace to those afar off, that is, to the Gentiles, as appears from many testimonies. For those who came to the faith from a Gentile origin had a greater claim to be called sons than those of Jewish origin. But it cannot be denied that the others received it too, and for this reason he added "and to them that were nigh."
Marius Victorinus
And he shall stand and feed in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God; and they shall abide:
for now shall he be great unto the ends of the earth. [4]
He carries out the shepherding Himself in the name of God the Father, for the two have one administration, so the name of the Lord Jesus is glorified and reaches the ends of the earth.

The prophet sees in this King a good shepherd who feeds his people in the strength of the Lord, and it was said of the Lord Christ: "He taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes" (Mt 7:9).

* The authority of His teaching was so great that it seized many of them and drove them to great amazement. Because of their delight in what He said, Jesus asked them not to depart until the end of His discourse. For not only did the hearers not leave Him after He came down from the mountain, but the whole multitude followed Him because of the greatness of the love He showed in His discourse. Most were amazed because of His authority. For when He spoke of those matters He did not point to another, as the prophet Moses did, but everywhere He showed that He is the One who has authority to give the decision. And when He laid down the laws Jesus added: "But I say unto you" (Mt 5:22, 28, 32, 34, 39, 44). And when He reminded them of the day of the last judgment He showed that it is He who will carry out justice, whether by punishments or by honors. This is what caused agitation among them.
St. John Chrysostom. Before His ascension Jesus came and spoke to His disciples, saying: "All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth" (Mt 28:18).

If the kings of the two kingdoms, Israel and Judah, and their princes and armies, could not protect them, the divine Shepherd guarantees the peace of His kingdom, and keeps His people, not from Assyria or Babylon, but from the devil and all the powers of darkness.
He is the marvelous Shepherd who raises up shepherds and gives them Himself to work in them and through them, until perfect peace is accomplished through His holy sacrifice.

5 And this man shall be the peace, when the Assyrian shall come into our land: and when he shall tread in our palaces, then shall we raise against him seven shepherds, and eight principal men. 6 And they shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in the entrances thereof: thus shall he deliver us from the Assyrian, when he cometh into our land, and when he treadeth within our borders.
And this man shall be the peace.
When the Assyrian shall come into our land: and when he shall tread in our palaces, then shall we raise against him seven shepherds, and eight principal men. [5]

(Verses 5-6) are a poetic piece of ten lines depicting the Assyrian invasion, against which a number of national princes are raised, seven shepherds and eight princes, so that the invader turns back to his country in failure. These princes unite together so that one ruler appears who delivers from Assyria.

The Lord Christ is called "our peace" (Eph 2:14), as He accomplishes peace between man and the Father, and also grants peace to the soul with the body, and peace among men, as among the nations. St. Hippolytus sees that Assyria here points to the Antichrist.

Assyria was the most dangerous enemy at that time, and here it points to the devil, the enemy of good, the opponent of the Church of Christ; but the enemy of good will surely be defeated, and the victory will be for the Church of Christ.

Who are the seven shepherds and the eight princes whom the new King raises up from among men? The number 7 points to perfection in this world, and the number 8 points to entering beyond time and passing into eternity. The servants of Christ ought to be perfect shepherds in the Lord, and heavenly kings not drawn away by the glory and riches of the world. Their law is "divine peace," for the Lord Himself is their peace. The Lord Christ said: "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid" (Jn 14:27).

The enemy of good does not cease to storm our inner land by every means, in order to seize it for himself, so that it becomes a kingdom of darkness instead of a kingdom of light. He wishes to tread in our palaces, and so defile our hearts, which are the temple of God, with the Spirit of God dwelling in them. The war is between God and the devil, and the battlefield is our inner depths; if we accept His shepherding we shall surely enjoy His victory.

The prophet Isaiah depicted for us the work of this King the Shepherd and His shepherding through His servants, saying: "Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in judgment. And a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind" (Isa 32:1-2). It is as though this heavenly King who became man has opened His side for us that we may hide in it when the winds and storms of the devil rage against us! He is our impregnable fortress, and a refuge for us in the midst of trials.

Theodoret, Bishop of Cyrus, sees in his commentary on Isaiah (Isa 32:1) that this text does not apply to Hezekiah or Josiah or Zerubbabel. [A person must understand the king to be Christ our Lord, and the princes to be the holy Apostles and those who succeeded them, as they were appointed to direct the churches. The blessed David proclaimed of them: "Instead of thy fathers shall be thy children, whom thou mayest make princes in all the earth" (Ps 45:16)].

* It seems to me that he points to the Apostles, who became teachers in her (in the Church). And in describing their authority, power and glory he says: "whom thou mayest make princes in all the earth" (Ps 45:16)... Remember that the Apostles went about the whole world, and became princes more sovereign than all the other rulers, and with more authority than the emperors. The emperors have their authority while they are alive, but when they die they have it no more; the Apostles have authority while they are alive, and it increased all the more at their death. And while the laws of the emperors have their force within the borders of their countries, the commands of the fishermen extend to every place in the world. The Roman emperor cannot issue laws for the Persians, nor the Persians for the Romans, while these Palestinians legislated for the Persians and the Romans and the people of Thrace and the Scythians and the Indians and the Moors and the whole world. Their laws remained in force not only while they were alive but also after their death, and those who submitted to them preferred to lose their lives rather than turn back from these laws.

St. John Chrysostom. And they shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in the entrances thereof: thus shall he deliver us from the Assyrian, when he cometh into our land, and when he treadeth within our borders. [6]
"The land of Nimrod" is another name for Assyria, and here it symbolizes all the evil nations.

Father Victorinus, Bishop of Petau, sees that Nimrod points to the Antichrist, and that the Lord Christ sends seven shepherds, who are the seven great archangels, to strike the kingdom of the Antichrist.

If the enemy has entered our land and trodden our borders, then through the direct shepherding of the Lord Christ, and His shepherding through His Apostles, the battle turns in our favor, and the kingdom of the devil collapses as by a sword, and we escape from his hand, repeating the words of the Savior: "Be of good cheer; I have overcome the world."

entries.section: 5. An ecumenical extension of the shepherding:

paragraphs.text: And the remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many people as a dew from the LORD, as the showers upon the grass, that tarrieth not for man, nor waiteth for the sons of men. [7]

After speaking of the Good Shepherd who chose His disciples and Apostles to work through them, and how the battle turned into victory for us and the collapse of the kingdom of the devil, the prophet presents to us a wonderful picture of the Church and her work on an ecumenical level.

She is "the remnant of Jacob," the very few who received faith in the Lord Christ, and enjoyed the descent of His Holy Spirit upon them on the day of Pentecost to be the leaven that leavens the whole lump. She goes forth "in the midst of many people," working by the Spirit of the Lord for the salvation of many from all nations and tongues and peoples. She is scattered throughout the world to be its salt and its light. By this the spiritual kingdom of Christ is established.

They are "as a dew from the LORD"; they do not work with a fanatical human mind, but with a heavenly mind that descends like dew from the Lord. They have been born from above, and so they offer heavenly things so that all may share with them the sweetness of the new heavenly life.

They are "as the showers (the rains) upon the grass, that tarrieth not for man, nor waiteth for the sons of men," that is, they do not rely on human support but on the free grace of God. They water others with the waters of the Spirit, like heavenly rain from the Lord, in which no man has any merit.

When he speaks to us of the new flock under the care of the divine Shepherd, he announces the spiritual victory full of sweetness, so that the Church in the world becomes like dew from the Lord and like the summer shower in beauty, gentleness, refreshment and radiance.

The remnant of Jacob is the spiritual Israel, or the company of true believers; they are like the divine dew, a secret of blessing and growth for many. These blessings do not come from men but are "from the LORD."

8 And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles in the midst of many people as a lion among the beasts of the forest, as a young lion among the flocks of sheep: who, if he go through, both treadeth down, and teareth in pieces, and none can deliver. 9 Thine hand shall be lifted up upon thine adversaries, and all thine enemies shall be cut off. 10 And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD, that I will cut off thy horses out of the midst of thee, and I will destroy thy chariots: 11 And I will cut off the cities of thy land, and throw down all thy strong holds: 12 And I will cut off witchcrafts out of thine hand; and thou shalt have no more soothsayers: 13 Thy graven images also will I cut off, and thy standing images out of the midst of thee; and thou shalt no more worship the work of thine hands. 14 And I will pluck up thy groves out of the midst of thee: so will I destroy thy cities. 15 And I will execute vengeance in anger and fury upon the heathen, such as they have not heard.

And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles in the midst of many people as a lion among the beasts of the forest, as a young lion among the flocks of sheep: who, if he go through, both treadeth down, and teareth in pieces, and none can deliver. [8]

In the preceding passage he depicted the Church in her gentleness toward the peoples because she offers living fellowship with God, yet she is strong in the Spirit, shattering and scattering the strongholds of darkness.

The prophet likened the believers at one time to dew, which softens and refreshes plants in an atmosphere of calm, and likened them also to the rains that water the fields, and now to lions among the beasts of the wilderness, whom all fear.

The believer is marked by pure love flowing from the depths as a gift of the Holy Spirit to him, and by firmness against evil, corruption and error. For this reason the Apostle Paul calls his disciple Timothy to strive as a good soldier of Jesus Christ, and the Lord Christ points to the strength of believers in the truth, saying: "which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist" (Lk 21:15). And the Apostle Paul speaks of the believers' resistance to the devil and his hosts: "the weapons of our warfare... mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds" (2 Cor 10:4-5).
Thine hand shall be lifted up upon thine adversaries, and all thine enemies shall be cut off! [9]

Victory is accomplished for the new Israel, so that she is like a lion, like a mighty warrior shattering her spiritual enemies. This battle is completed when God puts all enemies under the feet of Christ the Head of the Church (1 Cor 15:25-28).
The Psalmist sees the hosts of demons collapsing before the Church of God, and sings, saying: "the people fall under thee" (Ps 45:5).
And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD,
that I will cut off thy horses out of the midst of thee, and I will destroy thy chariots: [10]

When the Lord dwells in the heart and reigns, we do not need military power, but the great power of God. We repeat with all our strength: "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me" (Ps 23:4).

The secret of the Church's strength is the almighty Lord, not the human arm and human ability, so the Lord cuts off the horses from her midst and destroys her chariots, that she may enjoy the Spirit of the Lord, who lifts her from glory to glory, and she walks in the world like one ascending in a chariot of fire.

The Church, the new Israel, enjoys many divine blessings: 1. The removal of the material instruments of war, horses and chariots [10], so that the Church relies not on material things but on the surpassing grace of God. "And I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem" (Zech 9:10). 2. He cuts off from her the cities of the earth to give her heavenly cities, and throws down her temporal strongholds so that He Himself may be a wall of fire for her [11]. 3. The removal of vain worship with all its accompaniments of witchcraft and soothsaying [12]. 4. The removal of every idol in the heart, so that the Lord may set up His throne in it and occupy it completely [13]. 5. The enemy of good and his hosts fall under the divine wrath [15].
And I will cut off the cities of thy land, and throw down all thy strong holds: [11]

The Lord removes from His Church her earth, making her a second heaven in which He dwells. And He throws down all her temporal strongholds so that He Himself may be a wall of fire around her. It is as though their cities are turned from military cities into cities for dwelling, and the Lord guards them, for He is "their rock and their fortress and their deliverer" (Ps 18:2).
And I will cut off witchcrafts out of thine hand; and thou shalt have no more soothsayers:
Thy graven images also will I cut off, and thy standing images out of the midst of thee; [12]

The Lord removes from her all witchcraft and soothsaying (divination, or the claim to foretell future matters by the power of Satan), and opens her eyes by His Holy Spirit so that she recognizes the divine mysteries instead of the satanic works!
and thou shalt no more worship the work of thine hands. [13]
And I will pluck up thy groves out of the midst of thee: so will I destroy thy cities. [14]
The Lord removes the groves, that is, the wooden pillars set up as a symbol of Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Canaanites.
And I will execute vengeance in anger and fury upon the heathen, such as they have not heard. [15]
He concludes his discourse with a warning to whoever refuses to believe in the Savior, the Shepherd of souls, for he falls under the wrath and does not enjoy the heavenly blessings.
Who is there to shepherd me but You!
* Who else would shepherd my soul but You!
There is none who loves me and gives Himself for me but You!
The shepherding of men without You is destruction to my soul!
Your shepherding is unique and marvelous!
* You came to me in Beth-lehem, and made it the house of the heavenly Bread!
He who eats of You shall never hunger, and he who drinks of Your love shall never thirst!
You came to us, O Ancient of Days, O Eternal One, to carry me with You into Your eternity!
* You were born of a virgin, O Creator of the world!
And You have made of me, the servant, a little brother, and have given me sonship to Your almighty Father!
* You chose for Yourself disciples and Apostles, and made them princes and shepherds who bear the spirit of Your shepherding!
I see You transfigured in them, and I enjoy Your marvelous work through them!
You gave them authority over the powers of darkness.
By You they crushed the devil under their feet!
* You gave them Your Holy Spirit to shepherd Your people.
So they drew souls from all nations and tongues and peoples.
They became dew to the world, offering every fatherly kindness!
They became like the rain that turns wildernesses into a heavenly garden.
* They accepted to be lambs among wolves, devoured by the wolves, who then become gentle lambs!
You gave them the spirit of power to face error, so they became lions that are not afraid!
* By Your shepherding You gave Your people Your surpassing peace!
You cut off their horses from their midst and destroyed their chariots, for You became for them a heavenly wall of fire that keeps them!
You cut off all witchcraft and soothsaying, for You revealed to them the mysteries of Your heavens!
What a marvelous divine Shepherd You are!

1 Hear ye now what the LORD saith; Arise, contend thou before the mountains, and let the hills hear thy voice. 2 Hear ye, O mountains, the LORD's controversy, and ye strong foundations of the earth: for the LORD hath a controversy with his people, and he will plead with Israel. 3 O my people, what have I done unto thee? and wherein have I wearied thee? testify against me. 4 For I brought thee up out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed thee out of the house of servants; and I sent before thee Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. 5 O my people, remember now what Balak king of Moab consulted, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him from Shittim unto Gilgal; that ye may know the righteousness of the LORD. 6 Wherewith shall I come before the LORD, and bow myself before the high God? shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves of a year old? 7 Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, or with ten thousands of rivers of oil? shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul? 8 He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
Hear ye now what the LORD saith;
Arise, contend thou before the mountains, and let the hills hear thy voice. [1]
God asks the prophet Micah to arise and declare the controversy against the stubborn people, asking the mountains and hills to listen and follow the trial.
Chapters 6 and 7 depict a courtroom, where God judges in order to move His people to repentance before the great day of judgment comes.

The prophet Micah affirms that what he utters is not from himself, but that he drew it from God; he does not present a human word, but the word of the Holy God. For this reason it is fitting that they listen and give heed.

God calls the mountains and hills to stand as witnesses against His people, who built idolatrous altars on the high places, and offered sacrifices to strange, vain gods (1 Kgs 14:23; Jer 17:2-3; Ezek 20:27-28). Perhaps He means to bring the controversy against the inhabitants of those mountains and hills, which were immersed in idol worship.
Hear ye, O mountains, the LORD's controversy, and ye strong foundations of the earth:
for the LORD hath a controversy with his people, and he will plead with Israel. [2]

He cries aloud and does not keep silent (Isa 58:1), so that the foundations of the earth may hear him, for the matter is extremely serious. If the hearts of the people have become like hard rocks, God calls the rocks of the earth to listen and rebuke His people, because Israel has ears and does not hear.

"The LORD hath a controversy with his people": sin is turning the back to God, and so it becomes a cause of controversy with God. For this reason the Apostle Paul says: "when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God" (Rom 5:10).

If sin in general causes controversy with the Holy One, who cannot bear sin, it does so all the more when it proceeds from His people and His children, whom He wants to be holy to Him, as He is holy (Lev 20:26).

"He will plead with Israel," which some translate "He will reason with Israel": He wants to enter into dialogue with His people in order to affirm to them His gift of "free will," and so that they may look to His holy commandment not as an issued order they find hard, but as a work of love proceeding from a heavenly Father toward His beloved children.

* In many cases in the Holy Scriptures you see this picture, which is very astonishing and befits the tender love of God. He proclaims His ineffable goodness by showing that He wishes to enter into judgment with humanity in a wonderful manner.

St. John Chrysostom. * Thus He judges them, but hear what followed concerning the believers: "He will turn again, he will have compassion upon us" (Mic 7:19)... The Scripture says: "Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted" (Mt 5:5). And in another place the words: "He that believeth on me is not condemned, but is passed from death unto life, and he that believeth not is condemned."
Cassiodorus. O my people, what have I done unto thee?
and wherein have I wearied thee?
testify against me. [3]

God did not issue His judgment against His people, though He is the almighty Judge, but He asks to reason with them. He asks them whether He has wronged them in anything. By what do they justify their unfaithfulness to Him in spite of His surpassing faithfulness toward them.

It was not possible for the people to answer this question, because God, who is all love and mercy, has not wronged and never will wrong the people, nor any man, for He is the merciful Maker of good things, and if He permits affliction or chastening, it is for our proving or for our repentance and return to Him. He is not a harsh master, but a loving Father.

* Do you wish me to speak to you with the very words of God to stiff-necked and hard Israel? "O my people, what have I done unto thee? and wherein have I harmed thee? and wherein have I wearied thee?" This language is in truth more fitting for me to direct to you who have wronged me. It is grievous that we seek occasions against one another and break the fellowship of the Spirit that we have by differences of opinion, so that each has become more savage and violent against the other than the barbarians who are now fighting us, who have joined together against us by the Trinity that we divided... We have come to be at war, one against another, even against those of the one household. Or, if you will, we, members of one body, perish and destroy one another.

St. Gregory of Nazianzus. * "O my people, what have I done unto thee? and wherein have I wearied thee?" (Mic 6:3), showing their ingratitude, for while they enjoy all things, they meet Him with the opposite.
St. John Chrysostom. For I brought thee up out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed thee out of the house of servants; and I sent before thee Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. [4]

Since the people were silent for their inability to answer, God reviewed His dealings of love toward them from the time they were enslaved in Egypt, and how He sent them leaders supported by His grace: Moses, great among the prophets, and Aaron, the first high priest, and Miriam, the leader of the women, to create an atmosphere of joy through praise.
O my people, remember now what Balak king of Moab consulted, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him from Shittim unto Gilgal; that ye may know the righteousness of the LORD. [5]
God's care for His people continued in the wilderness, and how He kept them from the plots of Balak king of Moab so that they might cross over and enter the land of promise. He is faithful always.
The prophet Moses recorded the story of Balak and Balaam in the Book of Numbers (Num 22-24).

Shittim: the place where the children of Israel pitched their tents on the eastern bank of the Jordan before crossing the river to enter the land of promise (Josh 2:1). There the people received many divine commandments and promises. As for Gilgal, it was the first place where the people encamped after crossing the Jordan (Josh 5:3-3). There the people renewed their covenant with God (Josh 5:3-9).

St. Ambrose sees that God presents Himself to us as an example from which we learn, for even while rebuking His people He reminds them of His care for them when they were in affliction under slavery in a foreign land, burdened with heavy loads.
Wherewith shall I come before the LORD, and bow myself before the high God?
shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves of a year old? [6]

The Jews thought they were able to appease God by the multitude of sacrifices without practicing the spiritual life in their daily conduct. As though what concerns God were the offerings and sacrifices presented to Him in His temple, they did not realize that God seeks man himself: "My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways." God wants to prepare us to enjoy fellowship in the eternal glories. God wants us to offer living, reasonable sacrifices, acceptable to Him (Rom 12:1-2). Sacrifices of love from the heart, so that we return love to Him with love!
Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, or with ten thousands of rivers of oil?
shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul? [7]

Israel's first answer came in the form of three questions: First, is God pleased with the offering of ordinary calves as sacrifices? Second, will He multiply the sacrifices and offerings, so that he slaughters thousands of rams and offers ten thousands of rivers of oil? Third, will he offer extraordinary sacrifices, even if it leads to offering their firstborn (of their sons) as sacrifices, which the Law forbids (Deut 12:29-31; 2 Kgs 3:27; Judg 11:30-40)? For the sacrifice of the firstborn son had crept into Israel along with other sinful idolatrous practices.

It is clear that the sinner, however much sin attracts him, feels a deep emptiness in the depths of his soul, and wants to fill this emptiness by appeasing God, even if he offers all that he possesses, and what is most precious to him: his children! But the need is for the sanctification of the heart and mind and practical conduct in the Lord!
* God is not reconciled, nor are sins forgiven, by ten thousands of goats and thousands of rams or by the fruits of unholiness; rather the grace of the Lord shows the good life.

St. Ambrose. * Does everyone who turns from sin to faith turn from sinful practices (as if they were his mother) to life? I cite one of the twelve prophets, who says: "Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?" (Mic 6:7). Can a mother buy her way to God by offering her firstborn? This must not be understood as an attack on the words: "Be fruitful, and multiply" (Gen 1:28).

St. Clement of Alexandria. * When they were rebuked because they always lacked any other virtue, they excused themselves at first that they offer sacrifices, saying that they offer them continually. From here we understand why all the prophets exactly... reject this defense. For it is clear that the sacrifices were not established for their own sake, but as an instrument to suggest their conduct. So if they ignored their necessary obligations, occupied only with sacrifices, God said that He no longer accepts them (Amos 5:22; Isa 1:11-15).
Theodoret, Bishop of Cyrus. He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God? [8]

Israel thought it pleased God with animal sacrifices and the multitude of offerings, even to the point of offering human sacrifices, so the prophet arose to correct their concepts by moving them from preoccupation with animal sacrifices while practicing injustice to the practice of active love and walking humbly with the Lord.

As God was preparing the mind of His people to accept the Gentiles into the faith, the answer came general to any man in the world: "He hath shewed thee, O man," and He did not say "O Israel." The message is directed to all.

* Now, it is our duty to live the virtuous life, and God asks this of us; we do not rely on Him or on another, nor, as some think, on fate, but it is from our work, as the saying of the prophet Micah demonstrates: "He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy" (Mic 6:8).

Origen the scholar. * Who is so foolish as to think that God needs what is offered to Him for His own use? In many places He makes this idea foolish. So as not to trouble you, it is enough for me to quote this brief saying from the Psalm: "I said unto the LORD, Thou art my God: my goodness extendeth not to thee" (Ps 26:2). It is fitting for us to believe that God has no need not only of a flock or any earthly material thing, but not even of man's righteousness, and that any right worship offered to God is not for His benefit but for the benefit of man. For no one says that a spring benefits from his drinking of it, nor the light from his seeing it. In fact the ancient Church offered animal sacrifices, which the present people of God read about without imitating them, for these sacrifices mean nothing except that they point to what we do in order to cleave to God and urge our neighbor to do so. The sacrifice is a visible sacrament or holy sign of an invisible sacrifice.

* You ask: What ought I to offer? Offer yourself. For what does the Lord ask of you but yourself? For He created nothing among earthly creatures that is better than you. He asks of you yourself from yourself.

St. Augustine. * "God is good and exceedingly kind." He is merciful and gracious and rich in mercy (Ps 145:8). He does not desire the death of the wicked, but that he turn (Ezek 18:23). He is the Savior of all people, especially of those that believe (1 Tim 4:10). For this reason it is fitting for the children of God also to be merciful (Mt 5:7) and peacemakers (Mt 5:9), forgiving one another as Christ forgave us (Col 3:13), not judging lest we be judged (Mt 7:1), for a man stands or falls to God; who art thou that judgest another man's servant? (Rom 14:14).

Tertullian the scholar. * You have been told, O man, what is good, what does the Lord require of you but to do justice, and to love mercy, and to be ready to walk with your Lord? For this reason the Gospel says to you: "Arise, let us go hence" (Jn 14:31), while the Law says to you: "that you walk after the Lord your God." You have learned the way of escape from here; why do you delay?
St. Ambrose. * If God is fire, a consuming fire (Deut 4:24), then everyone who is straw, everyone who is wood, flees from the fire lest he be burned.2

St. Jerome. * He says: Forget your burnt offerings and your countless sacrifices, and the offerings of your firstborn.
